1.title: People in Successful Projects: Leadership, Change and Communication
1.text: Welcome to Module two: People in Successful Projects: Leadership, Change and Communication. It covers the exam area People management. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. two point one Assess an approach to leadership and management of teams. two point two assess an approach to leading change and to the people affected by the project. two point three apply communications and the people central to the method. two point four apply the communication management approach and the change management approach. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: People management (nine percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Leading and managing teams
1.text: Leading and managing teams. People are an element of the method in their own right: projects succeed or fail through people, and every exam scenario has people in it.

1.title: Leading and managing teams, continued
1.text: Leading and managing teams. The figure shows this: People at the center: team leadership, change and communication connected to the principles, practices and processes.

1.title: Leading and managing teams, continued
1.text: Leading and managing teams. Leadership inspires and guides people toward a goal. Management plans, organizes and controls the work within limits. A project manager needs both. The exam asks whether the approach fits these people in this situation.

1.title: Leading and managing teams, continued
1.text: Leading and managing teams. Style. Effective: Adapts to the person: more direction for a newcomer, more freedom for an expert. Not fit for purpose: One style for all; micromanages experts; abandons newcomers. Roles and goals. Effective: Clear roles, shared objectives, known authority. Not fit for purpose: Unclear roles; nobody sure who decides. Capability and competence. Effective: Gaps found early and closed by training, pairing or extra skills. Not fit for purpose: Work assigned regardless of skill; gaps found at delivery.

1.title: Leading and managing teams, continued
1.text: Leading and managing teams. Diversity. Effective: Different views invited and used. Not fit for purpose: One voice dominates. Trust. Effective: Problems raised early without blame. Not fit for purpose: Bad news hidden; blame culture. Several parties. Effective: Agreed ways of working across customer, supplier and remote teams. Not fit for purpose: Assumes everyone shares the same habits. Exam tip: Capability is what the team can do; competence is what one person can do. A named person lacking a skill is a competence issue; a team lacking capacity or tools is a capability issue.

1.title: Leading change and the people affected
1.text: Leading change and the people affected. Change management helps people move from the current way of working to the new one so that the benefits are realized. A project can deliver on time and still fail if nobody adopts the result. Two groups matter: people within the project (the project management team) and people affected by the project (users, operations staff, customers). A stakeholder can be either. The change management approach, a P I D product, says who is affected and how, how they will be involved, trained and supported, and how adoption will be measured.

1.title: Leading change and the people affected, continued
1.text: Leading change and the people affected. Impact. Effective: Analyzes early who is affected and how (berth agents lose paper permits). Not fit for purpose: Assumes people will adapt after delivery. Involvement. Effective: Affected people help design and test the service. Not fit for purpose: The change arrives as a surprise. Readiness and support. Effective: Training and time to adjust planned before go-live. Not fit for purpose: Training cut to save time or money.

1.title: Leading change and the people affected, continued
1.text: Leading change and the people affected. Resistance. Effective: Concerns listened to and causes addressed. Not fit for purpose: Resistance ignored or punished. Ownership. Effective: Senior user and executive visibly lead the change. Not fit for purpose: Left to the project team alone. Adoption. Effective: Use measured and linked to the benefits. Not fit for purpose: Ends at delivery. Exam tip: Delivering the product is not delivering the change. If the product is delivered but people do not use it, the gap is change management, led with the senior user.

1.title: Communication and stakeholders
1.text: Communication and stakeholders. Communication is two-way, planned and fitted to the audience. The communication management approach, also a P I D product, records who needs what information, when, through which channel, from whom, and how feedback is gathered. It rests on stakeholder analysis: identify stakeholders, analyze interest and influence, plan engagement, engage and review. The project manager owns it, and board members help by engaging the groups they speak for.

1.title: Communication and stakeholders, continued
1.text: Communication and stakeholders. Stakeholder analysis. Effective: Everyone within and affected is found, analyzed and kept up to date. Not fit for purpose: Only the board is listed; analysis done once. Engagement. Effective: Matched to each group: high influence and interest means close involvement. Not fit for purpose: The same message for everyone. Channel and frequency. Effective: Fits the audience: a short note for a busy executive, a briefing for harbor staff. Not fit for purpose: A long report to all; a channel nobody reads.

1.title: Communication and stakeholders, continued
1.text: Communication and stakeholders. Feedback. Effective: Two-way; gathered, answered and acted on. Not fit for purpose: One-way broadcast. Timing. Effective: Bad news and needed decisions travel at once. Not fit for purpose: Held back for the next scheduled report. The approach. Effective: Reviewed and changed as stakeholders change. Not fit for purpose: Written once and filed.

1.title: Communication and stakeholders, continued
1.text: Communication and stakeholders. Tailoring. A small co-located team may rely on daily conversation and a one-page approach. A large multi-party project needs formal channels and a written plan. Agile teams use daily meetings and visible boards, but stakeholders still need engaging. Exam tip: A one-size report is a red flag. If every audience gets the same document at the same time with no way to reply, the approach is not fit for purpose.

1.title: People central to the method and the Additional Information
1.text: People central to the method and the Additional Information. The people central to the method are the project management team (board, project manager, team managers, assurance and support) and the key stakeholders around them. The Additional Information in the exam describes some of them: skills, attitudes, time and preferences. Use each fact to choose the action.

2.title: People central to the method and the Additional Information, continued
2.text: People central to the method and the Additional Information. A very busy executive. Short, decision-focused reports; delegate through the project manager and assurance. A senior user who doubts the new service. Involve early, listen, show how concerns are met. A team manager new to the platform. More guidance, closer checkpoints, pairing. A supplier lead who reads only brief updates. A short written summary with the decision needed. Assurance staff who also work on the delivery. An independence problem: assurance must be independent of the project manager. A team split across two organizations. Agreed channels, regular check-ins, shared tools.

2.title: People central to the method and the Additional Information, continued
2.text: People central to the method and the Additional Information. Judge an approach in four steps: who the people are, what the situation is, what approach was used, and whether it fits these people. Then name the product that records it. Exam tip: If a question names a person, the Additional Information usually changes the best answer. Match the action to that person's skills, time, attitude or position.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. The Additional Information says Wei Chen's Delta Software developers are new to the permit platform. Sam Okafor gives them no guidance, saying strong teams need freedom. Was this appropriate, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: No, because the style should fit the team's experience and support needs. Effective team leadership adapts to the people's capability and competence, and newcomers need more direction and support.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Project Harbor will change how berth agents request permits, yet Sam Okafor plans no contact or training for them until after rollout. What should Sam do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Involve the berth agents now and plan their training and support. The change management approach should involve affected people early and plan training and support before go-live.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Sam wants to record which Project Harbor stakeholders need which information, when, through which channel and from whom. Which management product should hold this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The communication management approach. The communication management approach records who needs what information, when, how and from whom, plus the feedback route.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. At the start of Project Harbor, Sam lists only the project board as stakeholders and never reviews the list. Was this appropriate, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: No, because affected people are stakeholders too and the list needs review. Stakeholder analysis covers everyone who can affect or is affected by the project and must be kept up to date.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. The Additional Information says Lena Kovac, the senior supplier, travels often and reads only short written updates. Sam must tell her about a delay that needs her decision. What should Sam do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Send a short note with the delay, its impact and the decision needed. The channel and style must fit the person, and a decision that is needed should travel at once rather than wait for a meeting.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Which management product records how Project Harbor will help berth agents and harbor staff adopt the online permit service? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The change management approach. The change management approach says who is affected, how they will be supported and how adoption will be measured.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the difference between leadership and management? Answer: Leadership inspires and guides people; management plans and controls the work. Question two. Which three qualities of an effective team does the method stress? Answer: Diversity, capability and competence. Question three. What is the change management approach for? Answer: How the project helps affected people adopt the change.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does the communication management approach record? Answer: Who needs what information, when, how and from whom, and how feedback is gathered. Question five. Define a stakeholder. Answer: Anyone who can affect, is affected by, or believes they are affected by the project. Question six. Which document holds both approaches? Answer: The P I D.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Leadership and management: inspire people and guide them; plan and control the work. Team qualities: diversity, capability (team) and competence (person). Change: move people to the new way; involve early, train and support, measure adoption. Within and affected: project management team; users, operations staff and customers. Communication: two-way, planned, fitted to the audience, with feedback. Stakeholders: identify, analyze interest and influence, plan, engage, review. Approaches: change and communication management approaches, both parts of the P I D. Additional Information: facts about named people; use them to choose the action.
